comments.text:
Calling `stats::fisher.test` with crafted input results in a segfault due to an out of bounds write:

```
> stats::fisher.test(matrix(300000000L, nrow = 2L, ncol = 3L))

 *** caught segfault ***
address 0xbb3e1afceb60, cause 'memory not mapped'

Traceback:
 1: stats::fisher.test(matrix(300000000L, nrow = 2L, ncol = 3L))
An irrecoverable exception occurred. R is aborting now ...
[1]    12139 segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

The fault originates from an out of bounds write in `f2exact`, located in `fexact.c:401`, as reported by valgrind:

```
==12318== Invalid write of size 4
==12318==    at 0xBF4E300: f2xact (fexact.c:401)
==12318==    by 0xBF4E300: fexact (fexact.c:291)
==12318==    by 0xBF516CB: Fexact (fexact.c:2070)
==12318==    by 0x410265F: R_doDotCall (dotcode.c:763)
...
```

There's also a possibly related integer overflow reported by ubsan when running the same input:

```
.../R-devel/src/library/stats/src/fexact.c:1842:20: runtime error: left shift of 1800000001 by 1 places cannot be represented in type 'int'
```

Version:
```
svn rev r90590
```

OS:
```
Linux Ubuntu 26.04, aarch64
```

Also fails fataly on M1 Mac, although with a bus error.
comments.creator: adam.berkes2002
ikrylov

comments.text:
Hello,

(In reply to Ivan Krylov from comment #1)
> ...
> I've modified the function to be more careful about its allocation size
> calculations (tested with `make check-devel` on Linux). Do you think this is
> sufficient?

There is one check in the patch that doesn't seem correct:
```
@@ -239,6 +246,8 @@
     i3a = iwork(iwkmax, &iwkpt, nco, i_int);
     i3b = iwork(iwkmax, &iwkpt, nro, i_int);
     i3c = iwork(iwkmax, &iwkpt, nro, i_int);
+    if (kk > ((INT_MAX - k * 2) >> 1) || nco > (INT_MAX - 4*n2_stack) / 7)
+	prterr(40, "Workspace allocation size overflow (ikh > INT_MAX).");
     int ikh = imax2(k * 5 + (kk << 1), nco * 7 + 4*n2_stack);
     iiwk= iwork(iwkmax, &iwkpt, ikh, i_int);
     ikh = imax2(nco + 1 + 2*n2_stack, k);
```

specifically, the `k * 2`. The `int ikh` definition two lines below uses `k * 5`, which still allows for overflow, for example:
```
x <- matrix(0L, 2L, 32766L)
x[1L] <- 1L
stats::fisher.test(x)

.../src/library/stats/src/fexact.c:251:27: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 163845 + 2147418108 cannot be represented in type 'int'
```

Other than that the patch seems fine to me and passes my tests. Thank you for identifying and fixing bugs beside the one mentioned in my original report.
